speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: These additional contributions can then be used by employees to purchase their own insurance plans.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The PMBS makes healthcare costs more predictable and sustainable for employers.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: As the scheme's name suggests, employees can also enjoy portability of medical benefits where coverage continues with no risk of exclusions even if their employment situation changes.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: MediShield Life provides lifetime protection against large hospitalisation bills and selected costly outpatient treatments such as dialysis and chemotherapy, without exclusions for pre-existing conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Singaporeans who face difficulties in paying for their remaining medical bills after Government subsidies, insurance and MediSave can approach medical social workers at public healthcare institutions for further assistance.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: One is, there is some confusion on the ground, among friends, lay people and even some doctors, between insurance plans for Shield plan versus employee-benefit types of plans.

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: Is there a way to better educate our people on what exactly these different insurance covers are?

speaker: Dr Tan Yia Swam (Nominated Member)
text: My second question is: as the Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee (MHIC) is reviewing problems with the Shield plan providers and doctors, will there also be a way to relook how third-party administrators of employee-benefit plans could be better regulated?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Indeed, education is going to be key in terms of how we advise our employees to navigate between the insurance plans as well as the Shield plans.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I believe that is something that we can look into under the auspices of Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, we should be working with the tripartite partners, namely, the Labour Movement, together with the Singapore National Employers Federation (SNEF), ourselves, and, perhaps, even bringing in the Ministry of Health (MOH) to work together to collectively come up with very clear communication and educational principles and discussion groups, so that we can communicate some of these policies fairly, clearly and effectively.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: On plans to look at third-party administrators, again, this cannot just be isolated to one or two Ministries.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The third-party administrators have been in existence for quite a number of decades now.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: To work collectively to make sure that we find a more nuanced approach involves even the trade associations.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In this particular setting, we need to involve professional associations, for instance, like the Singapore Medical Association, and if you want, to even extend it to the Primary Care Network, probably the College of Family Physicians and, perhaps, the Academy as well, to get them involved in coming up with a more nuanced and middle-of-the-path kind of approach involving the providers, third-party administrators, payers and also the patients who are, ultimately, the end-user of the entire system.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, it is not something that we can decide in one Sitting.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Perhaps, it is something that the industry should come together and work towards.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: There are workers whose employer medical benefits come from an insurer.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In some instances, the employer's insurer changed and the new insurer no longer covered what the old insurer would cover.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: For employees who are so affected, how can they get help?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Often, they do not know until they submit a claim and they find that the terms and conditions have changed.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond PMBS, which the Minister has cited, are there other best practice recommendations which TAFEP, MOH and the Monetary Authority of Singapore can work on, so that the insurance industry can have a more consistent practice including providing avenues for workers to get help?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We certainly can step in to see how we can bring the parties together.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: But, today, there is no legal requirement for them to do so.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We obviously aspire that employers continue to take a very enlightened, engaging approach in terms of dealing with the medical benefits and the coverage for all of their employees, particularly when it comes to collective agreements.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And we hope that all parties would come together.
